top_choice_rationale: P002 (Helpman and Melitz) rests on a mature, general achievement. Melitz (2003) and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extension to exports versus FDI made firm heterogeneity, selection and reallocation central to trade theory. Their core predictions have been tested on firm-level and transaction-level data in many countries for over twenty years. I apply the same standard to every field, and by it P002 does better than P001, whose collateral channel is established mainly as a reusable modelling mechanism and not as a measured magnitude. P001 is a very close second. It has the cleaner two-author attribution, and I accept that the 2022 overlap is a citation-wording issue. Its support does not count as evidence of merit. P002's weaknesses are real but manageable by wording: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited, Krugman's 2008 prize covers the monopolistic-competition base, and Helpman's marginal credit must rest on the heterogeneous-firm extensions. The citation should therefore honour the theory of firm heterogeneity and selection and not claim the exporter-premium facts. I rank P003 third because it has a strong replication record, but the task-based and trade-shock strands may be two achievements and the China-shock magnitudes are still contested. I rank no award last because P001, P002 and P003 each describe a serious, mature contribution.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for P001, P002 or P003. The profile shows no tie to Helpman, Melitz, Kiyotaki, Moore, Autor, Hanson or Katz. My field of comparative institutions and measurement is not adjacent to these proposals. I am a Stockholm University colleague of IIES-affiliated members in a different department. My profile lists a Governance paper with 'Persson and Rothstein', and I cannot tell whether this is Torsten Persson, who is credited on B012. B012 is not in this slate. The 2024 presentation speech was delivered for the Academy and does not establish a preference. Conflicts are disclosed, not adjudicated.
